newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called to jump in Brent catch-up.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called to jump in Brent catch-up.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were called to open $3 higher on Thursday to catch-up with the late gains made on the Brent contract after OPEC members once more pledged themselves to respect their much-abused quota allocations.
Gas oil was expected to start around $163.25, to come into line with the market rise after it stopped trading yesterday, when it closed unchanged at $160.25.

Brent futures for August are anticipated slipping 5-10 cents as scepticism as to the merits of the OPEC announcement takes over, dealers said. SIMEX Brent was already quoted at $18.14, down eight cents on yesterday's IPE close of $18.22.
"I don't really understand why the market reacted to the OPEC pledges last night, they always pledge quota restraint and it never materialises," said one broker.
And he said that if the market had really believed OPEC could cut its 2 million barrel per day of over-production it would have hit $18.92, rather than calling a halt.
"There were enough sceptics around to hold back yesterday's rise," the broker added. "I can see us retreating back below $18 today on the Brent."
Mees Pierson's market report predicted further selling at the extremes on the back of OPEC news.
